notes:
WHERE IT IS: The list starts on n85.jpg (p. 74, rows 81–88) and continues on n86.jpg (p. 75, rows 89–119). n83 (p. 72) and n84 (p. 73) are East Coast text. n87 (p. 76) is 'Notes from the Stations'. The section heading is WEST COAST OF SCOTLAND. Rows 81–82 come straight under 'List of Stations', with no sub-heading, so their coast is null. The sub-headings, printed in small caps, are 'Outer Hebrides.' (83–88), 'Mainland, Skye, and Inner Hebrides.' (89–114) and 'Isle of Man.' (115–119). There are 39 stations, numbered 81–119.

COLUMNS: Returns in 5 years; * (sent returns in 1884); number; name and place; a class numeral I.–VI. (the 'value and brilliancy' the lead-in mentions); Feet (height); keeper. There is no flash or colour description, so character is null everywhere. I put the class numeral in 'other' rather than in character, because it is a rank, not a light's character. In 'printed', the leader dots are approximate and the braces are shown as { }. No station name is in italics. Only Bahama Bank has a type, '(L.V.)', printed in small caps. No row prints 'L.H.'.

CORRECTIONS TO THE OTHER READER'S DESCRIPTION: There is no Sanda in this list. Row 105 is 'Mull of Kintyre', VI., 297 feet. Rows with no feet printed are 92 Ardnamurchan and 93 Hynish (93's values sit on the brace it shares with 94). 118 Bahama Bank and 119 Langness print '?' for both class and feet. 117 Chickens Rock and 119 Langness have no returns figure.

BRACES: Hynish Signal Tower (93) and Skerryvore (94) are braced together. A single '5' on the left and a single 'II. 150 T. Dawson.' on the right serve both lines, so I gave both rows those values. Only 94 has the asterisk. Make sure T. Dawson counts as one keeper on the roll, not two. Within single stations, braces also group: two keepers at Cape Wrath (81) and at Butt of Lewis (83); two class numerals with one height at Stornoway (84, '2 lights'); and two numerals with two heights at Monach Isles (86).

COPIED AS PRINTED (not corrected):
- Kircudbright: modern Kirkcudbright.
- Wigtonshire: a period spelling.
- Chickens Rock: no apostrophe.
- Lochindaul: Loch Indaal.
- Island of Ghlais: Eilean Glas, Scalpay.
- Dhuheartach: Dubh Artach.
- Devaar: Davaar.
- Rhuvaal: Rubh' a' Mhail.
- Skervuile.
- Tyree: Tiree.
- 'A.Thompson.' is printed with no space.
- 'D.M'Culloch.' is printed with no space. The notes on p. 76 spell it 'Mr. McCulloch, Kyleakin'.
- 'J. Young-/clause.' is hyphenated across a line break. I joined it as 'J. Youngclause.'. The notes say he has since moved to an East Coast station.
- 'Frazer.' is a surname only.

I kept each keeper's final full stop as printed; strip it when building the roll if you want. 'Do.'/'do.' is kept as the place: 82 = Sutherland; 111–113 = Wigtonshire; 116–119 = I. of Man. The same keeper Wither is printed 'W. Wither' at 81 and 'Wm. Wither.' at 82, and the notes call Rhu Stoir 'Stoir Head'. 'Lismore I.' is taken as the name and 'Oban' as the place. 'Stornoway, 2 lights': the name is Stornoway, and '2 lights' is in other.

INCONSISTENCIES IN THE PRINT:
- The lead-in says schedules went to thirty-four stations, but 39 are listed.
- It says returns came from fifteen, but 17 rows carry the asterisk.
- 89 Rona shows '0' returns in 5 years yet is starred, and the notes on p. 76 quote a 1884 Rona return. So the 0 looks like a slip.
- 117 and 119 are starred but have no returns figure.
- 96 (Sound of Mull), 103 and 109 name keepers but have no asterisk.
